name: ranger
description: A self-directing engineering loop: give it one brief and walk away. A thin lead that never edits code drives model-tiered sub-agents (scout, planner, claims checker, reviewer, implementer, assessor, driver) through survey, triage, plan, claims-check, plan review, build, review, verify and commit, one local commit per item, until you stop it. Effort is sized to the item: a one-line copy fix costs two agents, a concurrency or migration bug gets the full adversarial pipeline and a mandatory fresh-eyes gate. Scouts map every tier of the codebase and sweep domain x lens pairs; pairs that come back clean twice go cold. On a maturing codebase it gets pickier rather than stopping: a quality floor that only rises, a capped backlog and a prune pass. UI items are driven in a real browser. `.ranger/FACTS.md` carries the repo's settled facts to every agent. Each invocation runs one cycle; keep it going with `/loop /ranger:run` or the bundled headless runner. `--preset` briefs (ui, ux, a11y, harden, perf) focus the sweep and `--dry-run` previews it. A PreToolUse hook hard-denies git push, remote mutation and PR creation. Blast-radius limits, no-progress quarantine and revert-on-reject keep an unattended run from turning into churn.
